Newtown Hospital

81 canyon Road

Newtown



21.09.2019



Dear Dr Macnor,



Re: Mr Jane Browne ,DOB: 25.08.2001                                                                         Comment [OET1]: Browne,



I am writing to refer Mr Browne, an 18 -year-old student, who has been demonstrated with                    Comment [OET2]: has
dermatological problem in his nipple.[space]Your definitive diagnosis and specialist management would
be appreciated.



Mr Browne was diagnosed with facial eczema while he was a baby in addition to flexular eczema in his
childhood period.



On 01.09.2019, Mr Browne came complaining of a tender, weepy and crusty nipple alongside surrounding
inflammation from due to the use of plaster dressing.That is why, he was advised to stop using it and       Comment [OET3]: put a space after the full
mepor dressing was recommended instead. He was asked to keep it uncovered except during sport.              stop
Hydrocortisone and soup substitute ware prescribed to him to manage his condition. 10 days later, he        Comment [OET4]: advised: asked less
showed signs of improvement.                                                                                formal
                                                                                                            Comment [OET5]: his nipple: using it
                                                                                                            confusing your reader here

Today, Mr Browne presented with his nipple unhealed nipple. He reported that, he had taken the              Comment [OET6]: hydrocortisone: it is a
hydrocortisone intermittently. On examination, the nipple was tender, warty and it changed in               generic name

appearance.                                                                                                 Comment [OET7]: were
                                                                                                            Comment [OET8]: no comma
                                                                                                            Comment [OET9]: altered/disfigured
Based on the above, My provisional diagnosis is either seborrheic keratosis or eczema.[space]Therefore, I
                                                                                                            Comment [OET10]: my
am referring him for your advice, assessment and treatment.



Should there be any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.



Yours sincerely,

Doctor
